mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day horizon are not statistically different from a pre-trend period (p > 0.05) or the 60-day return is positive despite the rate increase.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer pay growth (HOUST) indicate weakening labor market conditions, which typically precede S&P 500 declines over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while HOUST decreases over the same horizon
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) when the labor indicators show the described pattern.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% month-over-month suggests accelerating economic demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is negative or not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) when INDPRO shows the specified growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for three consecutive months suggests the Fed may maintain current rates, reducing discount rate expectations and supporting equity valuations, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is negative or the CPIAUCSL does not remain below 3% as predicted.

mechanism_narrative: When the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) falls below 4% while the Federal Funds Rate remains unchanged for two consecutive months, it signals a shift toward accommodative policy, which tends to boost equity valuations and drive positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and FEDFUNDS unchanged for two consecutive months
regime_hint: labor market tightness turning to slack
failure_condition: 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) or the policy conditions do not materialize as described.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in monthly pay growth (PAYEMS) exceeding 5% suggests wage inflation that outpaces productivity, creating excess labor costs and pressuring equity valuations, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is positive or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) when PAYEMS shows the spike.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining retail sales (not available in the provided proxies - skip this one) or alternatively, a sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below trend indicates supply-side weakness, which often precedes S&P 500 declines over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month's value for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward return is not negative or the decline in INDPRO does not persist as predicted.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the 10-year Treasury yield (not available in the provided proxies - instead use FEDFUNDS behavior) above 4% for 10 days suggests market expectations of future rate hikes, which typically weigh negatively on equity valuations and produce negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS remains above 4% for 10 consecutive days
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is positive or the yield does not remain elevated as forecasted.
